key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce protective coatings for Q235 steel, with wear performance dependent on service humidity.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology and coating microstructure.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and tribological behavior under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links higher porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate with increasing humidity.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear findings involve Si3N4 counterface balls and may not generalize to other contact materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
